This is the START button Menu

Here you can view the map and rules, 
and change game options.
* You cannot change skill settings here.



To switch to a different type of training, 
select TRAINING, then select the category 
you want to train in.

To quit training, select QUIT.

BASIC ACTIONS


Here you can practice movements and camera controls.
Movement controls are as follows:



Use the left stick to move.
Movement speed changes depending 
on how much you tilt the stick.



Press the × button to switch between 
standing and crouching.
Press the × button longer to switch between 
standing and lying down.


Press the × button while running to execute a roll.

Press the △ button while lying down to switch between 
lying face up and face down.

BASIC ACTIONS


Camera controls are as follows:




Use the right stick to rotate the camera.

Press the R3 button to move the camera angle 
to behind the character's back.


Quickly press the R3 button in twice to move 
the camera angle to behind the character's back 
and reset the vertical angle to the default setting.

ATTACK ACTIONS 1


Here you will learn the controls for attacking.




Each weapon is slightly different, but in general, 
the L1 button is used to aim and the R1 button 
is used to fire.
Press the ○ button to reload.
For more details, see the descriptions for each weapon.

ATTACK ACTIONS 1


Before getting to attack methods, 
let's look at how to distinguish between friend and foe.



- Distinguishing Between Friend and Foe -
To tell friend from foe in a Team Battle, 
look to see whether the character's name 
is displayed above them.
Allies always have their names displayed. 

Enemies' names will only be displayed 
when you aim a weapon at them.

In this training, you are assigned to the Blue Team.
The dummies in this stage are also divided into teams. 

Look at how their names are displayed.

You can attack enemies, 
but be careful: if you attack an ally, 
your weapon will be locked for a while.

ATTACK ACTIONS 1

Next, you will learn about the 3 attack modes:  
Auto Aim, Over-the-Shoulder, and First Person.




Auto Aim Mode

Auto Aim Mode can only be used if Lock-On 
Settings is Enabled in GamePlay Options.

This mode is good for novice players.
When you press the L1 button to aim the weapon, 
the crosshairs automatically lock on to an enemy 
within range. However, you cannot attack specific 
parts of the body.


While in Auto Aim Mode, "AUTO AIM" is displayed 
at the top center of the screen.




Press the □ button to switch to 
Over-the-Shoulder Mode, 
and the △ button to switch to First Person Mode.

ATTACK ACTIONS 1


Over-the-Shoulder Mode




When you press the L1 button to aim the weapon, 
the camera switches to a diagonal view 
from behind the character.



Use the right stick to adjust the aim. 
Push the R3 button in to switch the view 
between left and right.



Aiming is not as precise as in First Person Mode.

Press the □ button to switch to Auto Aim Mode, 
and the △ button to switch to First Person Mode.

ATTACK ACTIONS 1


First Person Mode




When you press the L1 button to aim the weapon 
and then press the △ button, the camera switches 
to the character's perspective.
Use the right stick to adjust the aim.


First Person Mode allows for 
a high degree of aiming precision.

Press the △ button to return to the previous mode.

ATTACK ACTIONS 1
Lock On Distance

Lock on distance in Auto Aim Mode varies
according to weapon.
Submachine guns have the longest range, followed
by handguns, assault rifles, and shotguns.
Other attributes also vary according to weapon,
such as destructive power and recoil.

Get to know the differences between each weapon
 and find ones that work best for you.

ATTACK ACTIONS 2
Here you will learn the controls for CQC.

* You need to equip the "CQC+" skill to use CQC. 
If you do not have it equipped, 
exit Training and equip the skill under 
"Skill Settings" in "Personal."

When you equip a weapon, a "CQC" mark 
on the lower right of the screen tells you 
that the weapon can be used with CQC.



Each weapon is slightly different, but in general, 
tapping the R1 button rapidly executes a melee attack, 
while pressing and holding the R1 button executes 
a grab attack.


While holding an enemy, you can move around, shoot, 
and perform a variety of other actions. 
Go ahead and experiment.

This is the START button Menu

Here you can view the map and rules, 
and change game options.
* You cannot change skill settings here.



To switch to a different type of training, 
select TRAINING, then select the category 
you want to train in.

To quit training, select QUIT.

BASIC ACTIONS


Here you can practice movements and camera controls.
Movement controls are as follows:



Use the left stick to move.
Movement speed changes depending 
on how much you tilt the stick.



Press the × button to switch between 
standing and crouching.
Press the × button longer to switch between 
standing and lying down.


Press the × button while running to execute a roll.

Press the △ button while lying down to switch between 
lying face up and face down.

BASIC ACTIONS


Camera controls are as follows:




Use the right stick to rotate the camera.

Press the R3 button to move the camera angle 
to behind the character's back.


Quickly press the R3 button in twice to move 
the camera angle to behind the character's back 
and reset the vertical angle to the default setting.

ATTACK ACTIONS 1


Here you will learn the controls for attacking.




Each weapon is slightly different, but in general, 
the L1 button is used to aim and the R1 button 
is used to fire.
Press the ○ button to reload.
For more details, see the descriptions for each weapon.

ATTACK ACTIONS 1


Before getting to attack methods, 
let's look at how to distinguish between friend and foe.



- Distinguishing Between Friend and Foe -
To tell friend from foe in a Team Battle, 
look to see whether the character's name 
is displayed above them.
Allies always have their names displayed. 

Enemies' names will only be displayed 
when you aim a weapon at them.

In this training, you are assigned to the Blue Team.
The dummies in this stage are also divided into teams. 

Look at how their names are displayed.

You can attack enemies, 
but be careful: if you attack an ally, 
your weapon will be locked for a while.

ATTACK ACTIONS 1

Next, you will learn about the 3 attack modes:  
Auto Aim, Over-the-Shoulder, and First Person.




Auto Aim Mode

Auto Aim Mode can only be used if Lock-On 
Settings is Enabled in GamePlay Options.

This mode is good for novice players.
When you press the L1 button to aim the weapon, 
the crosshairs automatically lock on to an enemy 
within range. However, you cannot attack specific 
parts of the body.


While in Auto Aim Mode, "AUTO AIM" is displayed 
at the top center of the screen.




Press the □ button to switch to 
Over-the-Shoulder Mode, 
and the △ button to switch to First Person Mode.

ATTACK ACTIONS 1


Over-the-Shoulder Mode




When you press the L1 button to aim the weapon, 
the camera switches to a diagonal view 
from behind the character.



Use the right stick to adjust the aim. 
Push the R3 button in to switch the view 
between left and right.



Aiming is not as precise as in First Person Mode.

Press the □ button to switch to Auto Aim Mode, 
and the △ button to switch to First Person Mode.

ATTACK ACTIONS 1


First Person Mode




When you press the L1 button to aim the weapon 
and then press the △ button, the camera switches 
to the character's perspective.
Use the right stick to adjust the aim.


First Person Mode allows for 
a high degree of aiming precision.

Press the △ button to return to the previous mode.

ATTACK ACTIONS 1
Lock On Distance

Lock on distance in Auto Aim Mode varies
according to weapon.
Submachine guns have the longest range, followed
by handguns, assault rifles, and shotguns.
Other attributes also vary according to weapon,
such as destructive power and recoil.

Get to know the differences between each weapon
 and find ones that work best for you.

ATTACK ACTIONS 2

Each weapon is slightly different, but in general, 
tapping the R1 button rapidly executes a melee attack, 
while pressing and holding the R1 button executes

While holding an enemy, you can move around, shoot, 
and perform a variety of other actions. 
Go ahead and experiment.

This is the START button Menu

Here you can view the map and rules, 
and change game options.
* You cannot change skill settings here.



To switch to a different type of training, 
select TRAINING, then select the category 
you want to train in.

To quit training, select QUIT.

BASIC ACTIONS


Here you can practice movements and camera controls.
Movement controls are as follows:



Use the left stick to move.
Movement speed changes depending 
on how much you tilt the stick.



Press the × button to switch between 
standing and crouching.
Press the × button longer to switch between 
standing and lying down.


Press the × button while running to execute a roll.

Press the △ button while lying down to switch between 
lying face up and face down.

BASIC ACTIONS


Camera controls are as follows:




Use the right stick to rotate the camera.

Press the R3 button to move the camera angle 
to behind the character's back.


Quickly press the R3 button in twice to move 
the camera angle to behind the character's back 
and reset the vertical angle to the default setting.

ATTACK ACTIONS 1


Here you will learn the controls for attacking.




Each weapon is slightly different, but in general, 
the L1 button is used to aim and the R1 button 
is used to fire.
Press the ○ button to reload.
For more details, see the descriptions for each weapon.

ATTACK ACTIONS 1


Before getting to attack methods, 
let's look at how to distinguish between friend and foe.



- Distinguishing Between Friend and Foe -
To tell friend from foe in a Team Battle, 
look to see whether the character's name 
is displayed above them.
Allies always have their names displayed. 

Enemies' names will only be displayed 
when you aim a weapon at them.

In this training, you are assigned to the Blue Team.
The dummies in this stage are also divided into teams. 

Look at how their names are displayed.

You can attack enemies, 
but be careful: if you attack an ally, 
your weapon will be locked for a while.

ATTACK ACTIONS 1

Next, you will learn about the 3 attack modes:  
Auto Aim, Over-the-Shoulder, and First Person.




Auto Aim Mode

Auto Aim Mode can only be used if Lock-On 
Settings is Enabled in GamePlay Options.

This mode is good for novice players.
When you press the L1 button to aim the weapon, 
the crosshairs automatically lock on to an enemy 
within range. However, you cannot attack specific 
parts of the body.


While in Auto Aim Mode, "AUTO AIM" is displayed 
at the top center of the screen.




Press the □ button to switch to 
Over-the-Shoulder Mode, 
and the △ button to switch to First Person Mode.

ATTACK ACTIONS 1


Over-the-Shoulder Mode




When you press the L1 button to aim the weapon, 
the camera switches to a diagonal view 
from behind the character.



Use the right stick to adjust the aim. 
Push the R3 button in to switch the view 
between left and right.



Aiming is not as precise as in First Person Mode.

Press the □ button to switch to Auto Aim Mode, 
and the △ button to switch to First Person Mode.

ATTACK ACTIONS 1


First Person Mode




When you press the L1 button to aim the weapon 
and then press the △ button, the camera switches 
to the character's perspective.
Use the right stick to adjust the aim.


First Person Mode allows for 
a high degree of aiming precision.

Press the △ button to return to the previous mode.

ATTACK ACTIONS 1
Lock On Distance

Lock on distance in Auto Aim Mode varies
according to weapon.
Submachine guns have the longest range, followed
by handguns, assault rifles, and shotguns.
Other attributes also vary according to weapon,
such as destructive power and recoil.

Get to know the differences between each weapon
 and find ones that work best for you.

ATTACK ACTIONS 2
Here you will learn the controls for CQC.

* You need to equip the "CQC+" skill to use CQC. 
If you do not have it equipped, 
exit Training and equip the skill under 
"Skill Settings" in "Personal."

When you equip a weapon, a "CQC" mark 
on the lower right of the screen tells you 
that the weapon can be used with CQC.



Each weapon is slightly different, but in general, 
tapping the R1 button rapidly executes a melee attack, 
while pressing and holding the R1 button executes 
a grab attack.


While holding an enemy, you can move around, shoot, 
and perform a variety of other actions. 
Go ahead and experiment.

Choose "all" (all players) or "team" (teammates only) 
with the left/right directional buttons and 
use the keyboard to enter a message.



Please refrain from sending messages 
that may upset other players.

This is the START button Menu

Here you can view the map and rules, 
and change game options.
* You cannot change skill settings here.



To switch to a different type of training, 
select TRAINING, then select the category 
you want to train in.

To quit training, select QUIT.

BASIC ACTIONS


Here you can practice movements and camera controls.
Movement controls are as follows:



Use the left stick to move.
Movement speed changes depending 
on how much you tilt the stick.



Press the × button to switch between 
standing and crouching.
Press the × button longer to switch between 
standing and lying down.


Press the × button while running to execute a roll.

Press the △ button while lying down to switch between 
lying face up and face down.

BASIC ACTIONS


Camera controls are as follows:




Use the right stick to rotate the camera.

Press the R3 button to move the camera angle 
to behind the character's back.


Quickly press the R3 button in twice to move 
the camera angle to behind the character's back 
and reset the vertical angle to the default setting.

ATTACK ACTIONS 1


Here you will learn the controls for attacking.




Each weapon is slightly different, but in general, 
the L1 button is used to aim and the R1 button 
is used to fire.
Press the ○ button to reload.
For more details, see the descriptions for each weapon.

ATTACK ACTIONS 1


Before getting to attack methods, 
let's look at how to distinguish between friend and foe.



- Distinguishing Between Friend and Foe -
To tell friend from foe in a Team Battle, 
look to see whether the character's name 
is displayed above them.
Allies always have their names displayed. 

Enemies' names will only be displayed 
when you aim a weapon at them.

In this training, you are assigned to the Blue Team.
The dummies in this stage are also divided into teams. 

Look at how their names are displayed.

You can attack enemies, 
but be careful: if you attack an ally, 
your weapon will be locked for a while.

ATTACK ACTIONS 1

Next, you will learn about the 3 attack modes:  
Auto Aim, Over-the-Shoulder, and First Person.




Auto Aim Mode

Auto Aim Mode can only be used if Lock-On 
Settings is Enabled in GamePlay Options.

This mode is good for novice players.
When you press the L1 button to aim the weapon, 
the crosshairs automatically lock on to an enemy 
within range. However, you cannot attack specific 
parts of the body.


While in Auto Aim Mode, "AUTO AIM" is displayed 
at the top center of the screen.




Press the □ button to switch to 
Over-the-Shoulder Mode, 
and the △ button to switch to First Person Mode.

ATTACK ACTIONS 1


Over-the-Shoulder Mode




When you press the L1 button to aim the weapon, 
the camera switches to a diagonal view 
from behind the character.



Use the right stick to adjust the aim. 
Push the R3 button in to switch the view 
between left and right.



Aiming is not as precise as in First Person Mode.

Press the □ button to switch to Auto Aim Mode, 
and the △ button to switch to First Person Mode.

ATTACK ACTIONS 1


First Person Mode




When you press the L1 button to aim the weapon 
and then press the △ button, the camera switches 
to the character's perspective.
Use the right stick to adjust the aim.


First Person Mode allows for 
a high degree of aiming precision.

Press the △ button to return to the previous mode.

ATTACK ACTIONS 1
Lock On Distance

Lock on distance in Auto Aim Mode varies
according to weapon.
Submachine guns have the longest range, followed
by handguns, assault rifles, and shotguns.
Other attributes also vary according to weapon,
such as destructive power and recoil.

Get to know the differences between each weapon
 and find ones that work best for you.

ATTACK ACTIONS 2
Here you will learn the controls for CQC.

* You need to equip the "CQC+" skill to use CQC. 
If you do not have it equipped, 
exit Training and equip the skill under 
"Skill Settings" in "Personal."

When you equip a weapon, a "CQC" mark 
on the lower right of the screen tells you 
that the weapon can be used with CQC.



Each weapon is slightly different, but in general, 
tapping the R1 button rapidly executes a melee attack, 
while pressing and holding the R1 button executes 
a grab attack.


While holding an enemy, you can move around, shoot, 
and perform a variety of other actions. 
Go ahead and experiment.

Open the Preset Codec Messages Menu and press 
the SELECT button again to open the Chat Menu.
This allows you to compose your own messages to 
other players in battle.


Choose "all" (all players) or "team" (teammates only) 
with the left/right directional buttons and 
use the keyboard to enter a message.



Please refrain from sending messages 
that may upset other players.

This is the START button Menu

Here you can view the map and rules, 
and change game options.
* You cannot change skill settings here.



To switch to a different type of training, 
select TRAINING, then select the category 
you want to train in.

To quit training, select QUIT.

BASIC ACTIONS


Here you can practice movements and camera controls.
Movement controls are as follows:



Use the left stick to move.
Movement speed changes depending 
on how much you tilt the stick.



Press the × button to switch between 
standing and crouching.
Press the × button longer to switch between 
standing and lying down.


Press the × button while running to execute a roll.

Press the △ button while lying down to switch between 
lying face up and face down.

BASIC ACTIONS


Camera controls are as follows:




Use the right stick to rotate the camera.

Press the R3 button to move the camera angle 
to behind the character's back.


Quickly press the R3 button in twice to move 
the camera angle to behind the character's back 
and reset the vertical angle to the default setting.

ATTACK ACTIONS 1


Here you will learn the controls for attacking.




Each weapon is slightly different, but in general, 
the L1 button is used to aim and the R1 button 
is used to fire.
Press the ○ button to reload.
For more details, see the descriptions for each weapon.

ATTACK ACTIONS 1


Before getting to attack methods, 
let's look at how to distinguish between friend and foe.



- Distinguishing Between Friend and Foe -
To tell friend from foe in a Team Battle, 
look to see whether the character's name 
is displayed above them.
Allies always have their names displayed. 

Enemies' names will only be displayed 
when you aim a weapon at them.

In this training, you are assigned to the Blue Team.
The dummies in this stage are also divided into teams. 

Look at how their names are displayed.

You can attack enemies, 
but be careful: if you attack an ally, 
your weapon will be locked for a while.

ATTACK ACTIONS 1

Next, you will learn about the 3 attack modes:  
Auto Aim, Over-the-Shoulder, and First Person.




Auto Aim Mode

Auto Aim Mode can only be used if Lock-On 
Settings is Enabled in GamePlay Options.

This mode is good for novice players.
When you press the L1 button to aim the weapon, 
the crosshairs automatically lock on to an enemy 
within range. However, you cannot attack specific 
parts of the body.


While in Auto Aim Mode, "AUTO AIM" is displayed 
at the top center of the screen.




Press the □ button to switch to 
Over-the-Shoulder Mode, 
and the △ button to switch to First Person Mode.

ATTACK ACTIONS 1


Over-the-Shoulder Mode




When you press the L1 button to aim the weapon, 
the camera switches to a diagonal view 
from behind the character.



Use the right stick to adjust the aim. 
Push the R3 button in to switch the view 
between left and right.



Aiming is not as precise as in First Person Mode.

Press the □ button to switch to Auto Aim Mode, 
and the △ button to switch to First Person Mode.

ATTACK ACTIONS 1


First Person Mode




When you press the L1 button to aim the weapon 
and then press the △ button, the camera switches 
to the character's perspective.
Use the right stick to adjust the aim.


First Person Mode allows for 
a high degree of aiming precision.

Press the △ button to return to the previous mode.

ATTACK ACTIONS 1
Lock On Distance

Lock on distance in Auto Aim Mode varies
according to weapon.
Submachine guns have the longest range, followed
by handguns, assault rifles, and shotguns.
Other attributes also vary according to weapon,
such as destructive power and recoil.

Get to know the differences between each weapon
 and find ones that work best for you.

ATTACK ACTIONS 2
Here you will learn the controls for CQC.

* You need to equip the "CQC+" skill to use CQC. 
If you do not have it equipped, 
exit Training and equip the skill under 
"Skill Settings" in "Personal."

When you equip a weapon, a "CQC" mark 
on the lower right of the screen tells you 
that the weapon can be used with CQC.



Each weapon is slightly different, but in general, 
tapping the R1 button rapidly executes a melee attack, 
while pressing and holding the R1 button executes 
a grab attack.


While holding an enemy, you can move around, shoot, 
and perform a variety of other actions. 
Go ahead and experiment.

- Chat -




Open the Preset Codec Messages Menu and press 
the SELECT button again to open the Chat Menu.
This allows you to compose your own messages to 
other players in battle.


Choose "all" (all players) or "team" (teammates only) 
with the left/right directional buttons and 
use the keyboard to enter a message.



Please refrain from sending messages 
that may upset other players.

This is the START button Menu

Here you can view the map and rules, 
and change game options.
* You cannot change skill settings here.



To switch to a different type of training, 
select TRAINING, then select the category 
you want to train in.

To quit training, select QUIT.

BASIC ACTIONS


Here you can practice movements and camera controls.
Movement controls are as follows:



Use the left stick to move.
Movement speed changes depending 
on how much you tilt the stick.



Press the × button to switch between 
standing and crouching.
Press the × button longer to switch between 
standing and lying down.


Press the × button while running to execute a roll.

Press the △ button while lying down to switch between 
lying face up and face down.

BASIC ACTIONS


Camera controls are as follows:




Use the right stick to rotate the camera.

Press the R3 button to move the camera angle 
to behind the character's back.


Quickly press the R3 button in twice to move 
the camera angle to behind the character's back 
and reset the vertical angle to the default setting.

ATTACK ACTIONS 1


Here you will learn the controls for attacking.




Each weapon is slightly different, but in general, 
the L1 button is used to aim and the R1 button 
is used to fire.
Press the ○ button to reload.
For more details, see the descriptions for each weapon.

ATTACK ACTIONS 1


Before getting to attack methods, 
let's look at how to distinguish between friend and foe.



- Distinguishing Between Friend and Foe -
To tell friend from foe in a Team Battle, 
look to see whether the character's name 
is displayed above them.
Allies always have their names displayed. 

Enemies' names will only be displayed 
when you aim a weapon at them.

In this training, you are assigned to the Blue Team.
The dummies in this stage are also divided into teams. 

Look at how their names are displayed.

You can attack enemies, 
but be careful: if you attack an ally, 
your weapon will be locked for a while.

ATTACK ACTIONS 1

Next, you will learn about the 3 attack modes:  
Auto Aim, Over-the-Shoulder, and First Person.




Auto Aim Mode

Auto Aim Mode can only be used if Lock-On 
Settings is Enabled in GamePlay Options.

This mode is good for novice players.
When you press the L1 button to aim the weapon, 
the crosshairs automatically lock on to an enemy 
within range. However, you cannot attack specific 
parts of the body.


While in Auto Aim Mode, "AUTO AIM" is displayed 
at the top center of the screen.




Press the □ button to switch to 
Over-the-Shoulder Mode, 
and the △ button to switch to First Person Mode.

ATTACK ACTIONS 1


Over-the-Shoulder Mode




When you press the L1 button to aim the weapon, 
the camera switches to a diagonal view 
from behind the character.



Use the right stick to adjust the aim. 
Push the R3 button in to switch the view 
between left and right.



Aiming is not as precise as in First Person Mode.

Press the □ button to switch to Auto Aim Mode, 
and the △ button to switch to First Person Mode.

ATTACK ACTIONS 1


First Person Mode




When you press the L1 button to aim the weapon 
and then press the △ button, the camera switches 
to the character's perspective.
Use the right stick to adjust the aim.


First Person Mode allows for 
a high degree of aiming precision.

Press the △ button to return to the previous mode.

ATTACK ACTIONS 1
Lock On Distance

Lock on distance in Auto Aim Mode varies
according to weapon.
Submachine guns have the longest range, followed
by handguns, assault rifles, and shotguns.
Other attributes also vary according to weapon,
such as destructive power and recoil.

Get to know the differences between each weapon
 and find ones that work best for you.

ATTACK ACTIONS 2

* You need to equip the "CQC+" skill to use CQC.

exit Training and equip the skill under

Each weapon is slightly different, but in general, 
tapping the R1 button rapidly executes a melee attack, 
while pressing and holding the R1 button executes 
a grab attack.


While holding an enemy, you can move around, shoot, 
and perform a variety of other actions. 
Go ahead and experiment.

This is the START button Menu

Here you can view the map and rules, 
and change game options.

To switch to a different type of training, 
select TRAINING, then select the category 
you want to train in.

To quit training, select QUIT.

BASIC ACTIONS


Here you can practice movements and camera controls.
Movement controls are as follows:



Use the left stick to move.
Movement speed changes depending 
on how much you tilt the stick.



Press the × button to switch between 
standing and crouching.
Press the × button longer to switch between 
standing and lying down.


Press the × button while running to execute a roll.

Press the △ button while lying down to switch between 
lying face up and face down.

BASIC ACTIONS


Camera controls are as follows:




Use the right stick to rotate the camera.

Press the R3 button to move the camera angle 
to behind the character's back.


Quickly press the R3 button in twice to move 
the camera angle to behind the character's back 
and reset the vertical angle to the default setting.

ATTACK ACTIONS 1


Here you will learn the controls for attacking.




Each weapon is slightly different, but in general, 
the L1 button is used to aim and the R1 button 
is used to fire.
Press the ○ button to reload.
For more details, see the descriptions for each weapon.

ATTACK ACTIONS 1


Before getting to attack methods, 
let's look at how to distinguish between friend and foe.



- Distinguishing Between Friend and Foe -
To tell friend from foe in a Team Battle, 
look to see whether the character's name 
is displayed above them.
Allies always have their names displayed. 

Enemies' names will only be displayed 
when you aim a weapon at them.

In this training, you are assigned to the Blue Team.
The dummies in this stage are also divided into teams. 

Look at how their names are displayed.

You can attack enemies, 
but be careful: if you attack an ally, 
your weapon will be locked for a while.

ATTACK ACTIONS 1

Next, you will learn about the 3 attack modes:  
Auto Aim, Over-the-Shoulder, and First Person.




Auto Aim Mode

Auto Aim Mode can only be used if Lock-On 
Settings is Enabled in GamePlay Options.

This mode is good for novice players.
When you press the L1 button to aim the weapon, 
the crosshairs automatically lock on to an enemy 
within range. However, you cannot attack specific 
parts of the body.


While in Auto Aim Mode, "AUTO AIM" is displayed 
at the top center of the screen.




Press the □ button to switch to 
Over-the-Shoulder Mode, 
and the △ button to switch to First Person Mode.

ATTACK ACTIONS 1


Over-the-Shoulder Mode




When you press the L1 button to aim the weapon, 
the camera switches to a diagonal view 
from behind the character.



Use the right stick to adjust the aim. 
Push the R3 button in to switch the view 
between left and right.



Aiming is not as precise as in First Person Mode.

Press the □ button to switch to Auto Aim Mode, 
and the △ button to switch to First Person Mode.

ATTACK ACTIONS 1


First Person Mode




When you press the L1 button to aim the weapon 
and then press the △ button, the camera switches 
to the character's perspective.
Use the right stick to adjust the aim.


First Person Mode allows for 
a high degree of aiming precision.

Press the △ button to return to the previous mode.

ATTACK ACTIONS 1
Lock On Distance

Lock on distance in Auto Aim Mode varies
according to weapon.
Submachine guns have the longest range, followed
by handguns, assault rifles, and shotguns.
Other attributes also vary according to weapon,
such as destructive power and recoil.

Get to know the differences between each weapon
 and find ones that work best for you.

Here you will learn the controls for CQC.

* You need to equip the "CQC+" skill to use CQC.

Each weapon is slightly different, but in general,

While holding an enemy, you can move around, shoot,

Go ahead and experiment.

ATTACK ACTIONS 1


Before getting to attack methods, 
let's look at how to distinguish between friend and foe.



- Distinguishing Between Friend and Foe -
To tell friend from foe in a Team Battle, 
look to see whether the character's name 
is displayed above them.
Allies always have their names displayed. 

Enemies' names will only be displayed

In this training, you are assigned to the Blue Team.

Next, you will learn about the 3 attack modes:  
Auto Aim, Over-the-Shoulder, and First Person.




Auto Aim Mode

Auto Aim Mode can only be used if Lock-On 
Settings is Enabled in GamePlay Options.

This mode is good for novice players.
When you press the L1 button to aim the weapon, 
the crosshairs automatically lock on to an enemy 
within range. However, you cannot attack specific 
parts of the body.


While in Auto Aim Mode, "AUTO AIM" is displayed 
at the top center of the screen.




Press the □ button to switch to 
Over-the-Shoulder Mode, 
and the △ button to switch to First Person Mode.

ATTACK ACTIONS 1

When you press the L1 button to aim the weapon, 
the camera switches to a diagonal view 
from behind the character.



Use the right stick to adjust the aim.

between left and right.



Aiming is not as precise as in First Person Mode.

and the △ button to switch to First Person Mode.

ATTACK ACTIONS 1


First Person Mode




When you press the L1 button to aim the weapon 
and then press the △ button, the camera switches 
to the character's perspective.

First Person Mode allows for 
a high degree of aiming precision.

Press the △ button to return to the previous mode.

This is the START button Menu

Here you can view the map and rules, 
and change game options.
* You cannot change skill settings here.



To switch to a different type of training, 
select TRAINING, then select the category 
you want to train in.

To quit training, select QUIT.

BASIC ACTIONS


Here you can practice movements and camera controls.
Movement controls are as follows:



Use the left stick to move.
Movement speed changes depending 
on how much you tilt the stick.



Press the × button to switch between 
standing and crouching.
Press the × button longer to switch between 
standing and lying down.


Press the × button while running to execute a roll.

Press the △ button while lying down to switch between 
lying face up and face down.

BASIC ACTIONS


Camera controls are as follows:




Use the right stick to rotate the camera.

Press the R3 button to move the camera angle 
to behind the character's back.


Quickly press the R3 button in twice to move 
the camera angle to behind the character's back 
and reset the vertical angle to the default setting.

ATTACK ACTIONS 1


Here you will learn the controls for attacking.




Each weapon is slightly different, but in general, 
the L1 button is used to aim and the R1 button 
is used to fire.
Press the ○ button to reload.
For more details, see the descriptions for each weapon.

ATTACK ACTIONS 1


Before getting to attack methods, 
let's look at how to distinguish between friend and foe.



- Distinguishing Between Friend and Foe -
To tell friend from foe in a Team Battle, 
look to see whether the character's name 
is displayed above them.
Allies always have their names displayed. 

Enemies' names will only be displayed 
when you aim a weapon at them.

In this training, you are assigned to the Blue Team.
The dummies in this stage are also divided into teams. 

Look at how their names are displayed.

You can attack enemies, 
but be careful: if you attack an ally, 
your weapon will be locked for a while.

ATTACK ACTIONS 1

Next, you will learn about the 3 attack modes:  
Auto Aim, Over-the-Shoulder, and First Person.




Auto Aim Mode

Auto Aim Mode can only be used if Lock-On 
Settings is Enabled in GamePlay Options.

This mode is good for novice players.
When you press the L1 button to aim the weapon, 
the crosshairs automatically lock on to an enemy 
within range. However, you cannot attack specific 
parts of the body.


While in Auto Aim Mode, "AUTO AIM" is displayed 
at the top center of the screen.




Press the □ button to switch to 
Over-the-Shoulder Mode, 
and the △ button to switch to First Person Mode.

ATTACK ACTIONS 1


Over-the-Shoulder Mode




When you press the L1 button to aim the weapon, 
the camera switches to a diagonal view 
from behind the character.



Use the right stick to adjust the aim. 
Push the R3 button in to switch the view 
between left and right.



Aiming is not as precise as in First Person Mode.

Press the □ button to switch to Auto Aim Mode, 
and the △ button to switch to First Person Mode.

ATTACK ACTIONS 1


First Person Mode




When you press the L1 button to aim the weapon 
and then press the △ button, the camera switches 
to the character's perspective.
Use the right stick to adjust the aim.


First Person Mode allows for 
a high degree of aiming precision.

Press the △ button to return to the previous mode.

ATTACK ACTIONS 1
Lock On Distance

Lock on distance in Auto Aim Mode varies
according to weapon.
Submachine guns have the longest range, followed
by handguns, assault rifles, and shotguns.
Other attributes also vary according to weapon,
such as destructive power and recoil.

Get to know the differences between each weapon
 and find ones that work best for you.

ATTACK ACTIONS 2
Here you will learn the controls for CQC.

* You need to equip the "CQC+" skill to use CQC. 
If you do not have it equipped, 
exit Training and equip the skill under 
"Skill Settings" in "Personal."

When you equip a weapon, a "CQC" mark 
on the lower right of the screen tells you 
that the weapon can be used with CQC.



Each weapon is slightly different, but in general, 
tapping the R1 button rapidly executes a melee attack, 
while pressing and holding the R1 button executes 
a grab attack.


While holding an enemy, you can move around, shoot, 
and perform a variety of other actions. 
Go ahead and experiment.

This is the START button Menu

Here you can view the map and rules, 
and change game options.
* You cannot change skill settings here.



To switch to a different type of training, 
select TRAINING, then select the category 
you want to train in.

To quit training, select QUIT.

BASIC ACTIONS


Here you can practice movements and camera controls.
Movement controls are as follows:



Use the left stick to move.
Movement speed changes depending 
on how much you tilt the stick.



Press the × button to switch between 
standing and crouching.
Press the × button longer to switch between 
standing and lying down.


Press the × button while running to execute a roll.

Press the △ button while lying down to switch between 
lying face up and face down.

BASIC ACTIONS


Camera controls are as follows:




Use the right stick to rotate the camera.

Press the R3 button to move the camera angle 
to behind the character's back.


Quickly press the R3 button in twice to move 
the camera angle to behind the character's back 
and reset the vertical angle to the default setting.

ATTACK ACTIONS 1


Here you will learn the controls for attacking.




Each weapon is slightly different, but in general, 
the L1 button is used to aim and the R1 button 
is used to fire.
Press the ○ button to reload.
For more details, see the descriptions for each weapon.

ATTACK ACTIONS 1


Before getting to attack methods, 
let's look at how to distinguish between friend and foe.



- Distinguishing Between Friend and Foe -
To tell friend from foe in a Team Battle, 
look to see whether the character's name 
is displayed above them.
Allies always have their names displayed. 

Enemies' names will only be displayed 
when you aim a weapon at them.

In this training, you are assigned to the Blue Team.
The dummies in this stage are also divided into teams. 

Look at how their names are displayed.

You can attack enemies, 
but be careful: if you attack an ally, 
your weapon will be locked for a while.

ATTACK ACTIONS 1

Next, you will learn about the 3 attack modes:  
Auto Aim, Over-the-Shoulder, and First Person.




Auto Aim Mode

Auto Aim Mode can only be used if Lock-On 
Settings is Enabled in GamePlay Options.

This mode is good for novice players.
When you press the L1 button to aim the weapon, 
the crosshairs automatically lock on to an enemy 
within range. However, you cannot attack specific 
parts of the body.


While in Auto Aim Mode, "AUTO AIM" is displayed 
at the top center of the screen.




Press the □ button to switch to 
Over-the-Shoulder Mode, 
and the △ button to switch to First Person Mode.

ATTACK ACTIONS 1


Over-the-Shoulder Mode




When you press the L1 button to aim the weapon, 
the camera switches to a diagonal view 
from behind the character.



Use the right stick to adjust the aim. 
Push the R3 button in to switch the view 
between left and right.



Aiming is not as precise as in First Person Mode.

Press the □ button to switch to Auto Aim Mode, 
and the △ button to switch to First Person Mode.

ATTACK ACTIONS 1


First Person Mode




When you press the L1 button to aim the weapon 
and then press the △ button, the camera switches 
to the character's perspective.
Use the right stick to adjust the aim.


First Person Mode allows for 
a high degree of aiming precision.

Press the △ button to return to the previous mode.

ATTACK ACTIONS 1
Lock On Distance

Lock on distance in Auto Aim Mode varies
according to weapon.
Submachine guns have the longest range, followed
by handguns, assault rifles, and shotguns.
Other attributes also vary according to weapon,
such as destructive power and recoil.

Get to know the differences between each weapon
 and find ones that work best for you.

ATTACK ACTIONS 2

Each weapon is slightly different, but in general, 
tapping the R1 button rapidly executes a melee attack, 
while pressing and holding the R1 button executes

While holding an enemy, you can move around, shoot, 
and perform a variety of other actions. 
Go ahead and experiment.

This is the START button Menu

Here you can view the map and rules, 
and change game options.
* You cannot change skill settings here.



To switch to a different type of training, 
select TRAINING, then select the category 
you want to train in.

To quit training, select QUIT.

BASIC ACTIONS


Here you can practice movements and camera controls.
Movement controls are as follows:



Use the left stick to move.
Movement speed changes depending 
on how much you tilt the stick.



Press the × button to switch between 
standing and crouching.
Press the × button longer to switch between 
standing and lying down.


Press the × button while running to execute a roll.

Press the △ button while lying down to switch between 
lying face up and face down.

BASIC ACTIONS


Camera controls are as follows:




Use the right stick to rotate the camera.

Press the R3 button to move the camera angle 
to behind the character's back.


Quickly press the R3 button in twice to move 
the camera angle to behind the character's back 
and reset the vertical angle to the default setting.

ATTACK ACTIONS 1


Here you will learn the controls for attacking.




Each weapon is slightly different, but in general, 
the L1 button is used to aim and the R1 button 
is used to fire.
Press the ○ button to reload.
For more details, see the descriptions for each weapon.

ATTACK ACTIONS 1


Before getting to attack methods, 
let's look at how to distinguish between friend and foe.



- Distinguishing Between Friend and Foe -
To tell friend from foe in a Team Battle, 
look to see whether the character's name 
is displayed above them.
Allies always have their names displayed. 

Enemies' names will only be displayed 
when you aim a weapon at them.

In this training, you are assigned to the Blue Team.
The dummies in this stage are also divided into teams. 

Look at how their names are displayed.

You can attack enemies, 
but be careful: if you attack an ally, 
your weapon will be locked for a while.

ATTACK ACTIONS 1

Next, you will learn about the 3 attack modes:  
Auto Aim, Over-the-Shoulder, and First Person.




Auto Aim Mode

Auto Aim Mode can only be used if Lock-On 
Settings is Enabled in GamePlay Options.

This mode is good for novice players.
When you press the L1 button to aim the weapon, 
the crosshairs automatically lock on to an enemy 
within range. However, you cannot attack specific 
parts of the body.


While in Auto Aim Mode, "AUTO AIM" is displayed 
at the top center of the screen.




Press the □ button to switch to 
Over-the-Shoulder Mode, 
and the △ button to switch to First Person Mode.

ATTACK ACTIONS 1


Over-the-Shoulder Mode




When you press the L1 button to aim the weapon, 
the camera switches to a diagonal view 
from behind the character.



Use the right stick to adjust the aim. 
Push the R3 button in to switch the view 
between left and right.



Aiming is not as precise as in First Person Mode.

Press the □ button to switch to Auto Aim Mode, 
and the △ button to switch to First Person Mode.

ATTACK ACTIONS 1


First Person Mode




When you press the L1 button to aim the weapon 
and then press the △ button, the camera switches 
to the character's perspective.
Use the right stick to adjust the aim.


First Person Mode allows for 
a high degree of aiming precision.

Press the △ button to return to the previous mode.

ATTACK ACTIONS 1
Lock On Distance

Lock on distance in Auto Aim Mode varies
according to weapon.
Submachine guns have the longest range, followed
by handguns, assault rifles, and shotguns.
Other attributes also vary according to weapon,
such as destructive power and recoil.

Get to know the differences between each weapon
 and find ones that work best for you.

ATTACK ACTIONS 2
Here you will learn the controls for CQC.

* You need to equip the "CQC+" skill to use CQC. 
If you do not have it equipped, 
exit Training and equip the skill under 
"Skill Settings" in "Personal."

When you equip a weapon, a "CQC" mark 
on the lower right of the screen tells you 
that the weapon can be used with CQC.



Each weapon is slightly different, but in general, 
tapping the R1 button rapidly executes a melee attack, 
while pressing and holding the R1 button executes 
a grab attack.


While holding an enemy, you can move around, shoot, 
and perform a variety of other actions. 
Go ahead and experiment.

Choose "all" (all players) or "team" (teammates only) 
with the left/right directional buttons and 
use the keyboard to enter a message.



Please refrain from sending messages 
that may upset other players.

This is the START button Menu

Here you can view the map and rules, 
and change game options.
* You cannot change skill settings here.



To switch to a different type of training, 
select TRAINING, then select the category 
you want to train in.

To quit training, select QUIT.

BASIC ACTIONS


Here you can practice movements and camera controls.
Movement controls are as follows:



Use the left stick to move.
Movement speed changes depending 
on how much you tilt the stick.



Press the × button to switch between 
standing and crouching.
Press the × button longer to switch between 
standing and lying down.


Press the × button while running to execute a roll.

Press the △ button while lying down to switch between 
lying face up and face down.

BASIC ACTIONS


Camera controls are as follows:




Use the right stick to rotate the camera.

Press the R3 button to move the camera angle 
to behind the character's back.


Quickly press the R3 button in twice to move 
the camera angle to behind the character's back 
and reset the vertical angle to the default setting.

ATTACK ACTIONS 1


Here you will learn the controls for attacking.




Each weapon is slightly different, but in general, 
the L1 button is used to aim and the R1 button 
is used to fire.
Press the ○ button to reload.
For more details, see the descriptions for each weapon.

ATTACK ACTIONS 1


Before getting to attack methods, 
let's look at how to distinguish between friend and foe.



- Distinguishing Between Friend and Foe -
To tell friend from foe in a Team Battle, 
look to see whether the character's name 
is displayed above them.
Allies always have their names displayed. 

Enemies' names will only be displayed 
when you aim a weapon at them.

In this training, you are assigned to the Blue Team.
The dummies in this stage are also divided into teams. 

Look at how their names are displayed.

You can attack enemies, 
but be careful: if you attack an ally, 
your weapon will be locked for a while.

ATTACK ACTIONS 1

Next, you will learn about the 3 attack modes:  
Auto Aim, Over-the-Shoulder, and First Person.




Auto Aim Mode

Auto Aim Mode can only be used if Lock-On 
Settings is Enabled in GamePlay Options.

This mode is good for novice players.
When you press the L1 button to aim the weapon, 
the crosshairs automatically lock on to an enemy 
within range. However, you cannot attack specific 
parts of the body.


While in Auto Aim Mode, "AUTO AIM" is displayed 
at the top center of the screen.




Press the □ button to switch to 
Over-the-Shoulder Mode, 
and the △ button to switch to First Person Mode.

ATTACK ACTIONS 1


Over-the-Shoulder Mode




When you press the L1 button to aim the weapon, 
the camera switches to a diagonal view 
from behind the character.



Use the right stick to adjust the aim. 
Push the R3 button in to switch the view 
between left and right.



Aiming is not as precise as in First Person Mode.

Press the □ button to switch to Auto Aim Mode, 
and the △ button to switch to First Person Mode.

ATTACK ACTIONS 1


First Person Mode




When you press the L1 button to aim the weapon 
and then press the △ button, the camera switches 
to the character's perspective.
Use the right stick to adjust the aim.


First Person Mode allows for 
a high degree of aiming precision.

Press the △ button to return to the previous mode.

ATTACK ACTIONS 1
Lock On Distance

Lock on distance in Auto Aim Mode varies
according to weapon.
Submachine guns have the longest range, followed
by handguns, assault rifles, and shotguns.
Other attributes also vary according to weapon,
such as destructive power and recoil.

Get to know the differences between each weapon
 and find ones that work best for you.

ATTACK ACTIONS 2
Here you will learn the controls for CQC.

* You need to equip the "CQC+" skill to use CQC. 
If you do not have it equipped, 
exit Training and equip the skill under 
"Skill Settings" in "Personal."

When you equip a weapon, a "CQC" mark 
on the lower right of the screen tells you 
that the weapon can be used with CQC.



Each weapon is slightly different, but in general, 
tapping the R1 button rapidly executes a melee attack, 
while pressing and holding the R1 button executes 
a grab attack.


While holding an enemy, you can move around, shoot, 
and perform a variety of other actions. 
Go ahead and experiment.

Open the Preset Codec Messages Menu and press 
the SELECT button again to open the Chat Menu.
This allows you to compose your own messages to 
other players in battle.


Choose "all" (all players) or "team" (teammates only) 
with the left/right directional buttons and 
use the keyboard to enter a message.



Please refrain from sending messages 
that may upset other players.

This is the START button Menu

Here you can view the map and rules, 
and change game options.
* You cannot change skill settings here.



To switch to a different type of training, 
select TRAINING, then select the category 
you want to train in.

To quit training, select QUIT.

BASIC ACTIONS


Here you can practice movements and camera controls.
Movement controls are as follows:



Use the left stick to move.
Movement speed changes depending 
on how much you tilt the stick.



Press the × button to switch between 
standing and crouching.
Press the × button longer to switch between 
standing and lying down.


Press the × button while running to execute a roll.

Press the △ button while lying down to switch between 
lying face up and face down.

BASIC ACTIONS


Camera controls are as follows:




Use the right stick to rotate the camera.

Press the R3 button to move the camera angle 
to behind the character's back.


Quickly press the R3 button in twice to move 
the camera angle to behind the character's back 
and reset the vertical angle to the default setting.

ATTACK ACTIONS 1


Here you will learn the controls for attacking.




Each weapon is slightly different, but in general, 
the L1 button is used to aim and the R1 button 
is used to fire.
Press the ○ button to reload.
For more details, see the descriptions for each weapon.

ATTACK ACTIONS 1


Before getting to attack methods, 
let's look at how to distinguish between friend and foe.



- Distinguishing Between Friend and Foe -
To tell friend from foe in a Team Battle, 
look to see whether the character's name 
is displayed above them.
Allies always have their names displayed. 

Enemies' names will only be displayed 
when you aim a weapon at them.

In this training, you are assigned to the Blue Team.
The dummies in this stage are also divided into teams. 

Look at how their names are displayed.

You can attack enemies, 
but be careful: if you attack an ally, 
your weapon will be locked for a while.

ATTACK ACTIONS 1

Next, you will learn about the 3 attack modes:  
Auto Aim, Over-the-Shoulder, and First Person.




Auto Aim Mode

Auto Aim Mode can only be used if Lock-On 
Settings is Enabled in GamePlay Options.

This mode is good for novice players.
When you press the L1 button to aim the weapon, 
the crosshairs automatically lock on to an enemy 
within range. However, you cannot attack specific 
parts of the body.


While in Auto Aim Mode, "AUTO AIM" is displayed 
at the top center of the screen.




Press the □ button to switch to 
Over-the-Shoulder Mode, 
and the △ button to switch to First Person Mode.

ATTACK ACTIONS 1


Over-the-Shoulder Mode




When you press the L1 button to aim the weapon, 
the camera switches to a diagonal view 
from behind the character.



Use the right stick to adjust the aim. 
Push the R3 button in to switch the view 
between left and right.



Aiming is not as precise as in First Person Mode.

Press the □ button to switch to Auto Aim Mode, 
and the △ button to switch to First Person Mode.

ATTACK ACTIONS 1


First Person Mode




When you press the L1 button to aim the weapon 
and then press the △ button, the camera switches 
to the character's perspective.
Use the right stick to adjust the aim.


First Person Mode allows for 
a high degree of aiming precision.

Press the △ button to return to the previous mode.

ATTACK ACTIONS 1
Lock On Distance

Lock on distance in Auto Aim Mode varies
according to weapon.
Submachine guns have the longest range, followed
by handguns, assault rifles, and shotguns.
Other attributes also vary according to weapon,
such as destructive power and recoil.

Get to know the differences between each weapon
 and find ones that work best for you.

ATTACK ACTIONS 2
Here you will learn the controls for CQC.

* You need to equip the "CQC+" skill to use CQC. 
If you do not have it equipped, 
exit Training and equip the skill under 
"Skill Settings" in "Personal."

When you equip a weapon, a "CQC" mark 
on the lower right of the screen tells you 
that the weapon can be used with CQC.



Each weapon is slightly different, but in general, 
tapping the R1 button rapidly executes a melee attack, 
while pressing and holding the R1 button executes 
a grab attack.


While holding an enemy, you can move around, shoot, 
and perform a variety of other actions. 
Go ahead and experiment.

- Chat -




Open the Preset Codec Messages Menu and press 
the SELECT button again to open the Chat Menu.
This allows you to compose your own messages to 
other players in battle.


Choose "all" (all players) or "team" (teammates only) 
with the left/right directional buttons and 
use the keyboard to enter a message.



Please refrain from sending messages 
that may upset other players.

This is the START button Menu

Here you can view the map and rules, 
and change game options.
* You cannot change skill settings here.



To switch to a different type of training, 
select TRAINING, then select the category 
you want to train in.

To quit training, select QUIT.

BASIC ACTIONS


Here you can practice movements and camera controls.
Movement controls are as follows:



Use the left stick to move.
Movement speed changes depending 
on how much you tilt the stick.



Press the × button to switch between 
standing and crouching.
Press the × button longer to switch between 
standing and lying down.


Press the × button while running to execute a roll.

Press the △ button while lying down to switch between 
lying face up and face down.

BASIC ACTIONS


Camera controls are as follows:




Use the right stick to rotate the camera.

Press the R3 button to move the camera angle 
to behind the character's back.


Quickly press the R3 button in twice to move 
the camera angle to behind the character's back 
and reset the vertical angle to the default setting.

ATTACK ACTIONS 1


Here you will learn the controls for attacking.




Each weapon is slightly different, but in general, 
the L1 button is used to aim and the R1 button 
is used to fire.
Press the ○ button to reload.
For more details, see the descriptions for each weapon.

ATTACK ACTIONS 1


Before getting to attack methods, 
let's look at how to distinguish between friend and foe.



- Distinguishing Between Friend and Foe -
To tell friend from foe in a Team Battle, 
look to see whether the character's name 
is displayed above them.
Allies always have their names displayed. 

Enemies' names will only be displayed 
when you aim a weapon at them.

In this training, you are assigned to the Blue Team.
The dummies in this stage are also divided into teams. 

Look at how their names are displayed.

You can attack enemies, 
but be careful: if you attack an ally, 
your weapon will be locked for a while.

ATTACK ACTIONS 1

Next, you will learn about the 3 attack modes:  
Auto Aim, Over-the-Shoulder, and First Person.




Auto Aim Mode

Auto Aim Mode can only be used if Lock-On 
Settings is Enabled in GamePlay Options.

This mode is good for novice players.
When you press the L1 button to aim the weapon, 
the crosshairs automatically lock on to an enemy 
within range. However, you cannot attack specific 
parts of the body.


While in Auto Aim Mode, "AUTO AIM" is displayed 
at the top center of the screen.




Press the □ button to switch to 
Over-the-Shoulder Mode, 
and the △ button to switch to First Person Mode.

ATTACK ACTIONS 1


Over-the-Shoulder Mode




When you press the L1 button to aim the weapon, 
the camera switches to a diagonal view 
from behind the character.



Use the right stick to adjust the aim. 
Push the R3 button in to switch the view 
between left and right.



Aiming is not as precise as in First Person Mode.

Press the □ button to switch to Auto Aim Mode, 
and the △ button to switch to First Person Mode.

ATTACK ACTIONS 1


First Person Mode




When you press the L1 button to aim the weapon 
and then press the △ button, the camera switches 
to the character's perspective.
Use the right stick to adjust the aim.


First Person Mode allows for 
a high degree of aiming precision.

Press the △ button to return to the previous mode.

ATTACK ACTIONS 1
Lock On Distance

Lock on distance in Auto Aim Mode varies
according to weapon.
Submachine guns have the longest range, followed
by handguns, assault rifles, and shotguns.
Other attributes also vary according to weapon,
such as destructive power and recoil.

Get to know the differences between each weapon
 and find ones that work best for you.

ATTACK ACTIONS 2

* You need to equip the "CQC+" skill to use CQC.

exit Training and equip the skill under

Each weapon is slightly different, but in general, 
tapping the R1 button rapidly executes a melee attack, 
while pressing and holding the R1 button executes 
a grab attack.


While holding an enemy, you can move around, shoot, 
and perform a variety of other actions. 
Go ahead and experiment.

use the R2 button for weapons and the L2 button for items.

and controls in this window.

the R2 button or the L2 button.

This is the START button Menu

Here you can view the map and rules, 
and change game options.
* You cannot change skill settings here.



To switch to a different type of training, 
select TRAINING, then select the category 
you want to train in.

To quit training, select QUIT.

BASIC ACTIONS


Here you can practice movements and camera controls.
Movement controls are as follows:



Use the left stick to move.
Movement speed changes depending 
on how much you tilt the stick.



Press the × button to switch between 
standing and crouching.
Press the × button longer to switch between 
standing and lying down.


Press the × button while running to execute a roll.

Press the △ button while lying down to switch between 
lying face up and face down.

BASIC ACTIONS


Camera controls are as follows:




Use the right stick to rotate the camera.

Press the R3 button to move the camera angle 
to behind the character's back.


Quickly press the R3 button in twice to move 
the camera angle to behind the character's back 
and reset the vertical angle to the default setting.

ATTACK ACTIONS 1


Here you will learn the controls for attacking.




Each weapon is slightly different, but in general, 
the L1 button is used to aim and the R1 button 
is used to fire.
Press the ○ button to reload.
For more details, see the descriptions for each weapon.

ATTACK ACTIONS 1


Before getting to attack methods, 
let's look at how to distinguish between friend and foe.



- Distinguishing Between Friend and Foe -
To tell friend from foe in a Team Battle, 
look to see whether the character's name 
is displayed above them.
Allies always have their names displayed. 

Enemies' names will only be displayed 
when you aim a weapon at them.

In this training, you are assigned to the Blue Team.
The dummies in this stage are also divided into teams. 

Look at how their names are displayed.

You can attack enemies, 
but be careful: if you attack an ally, 
your weapon will be locked for a while.

ATTACK ACTIONS 1

Next, you will learn about the 3 attack modes:  
Auto Aim, Over-the-Shoulder, and First Person.




Auto Aim Mode

Auto Aim Mode can only be used if Lock-On 
Settings is Enabled in GamePlay Options.

This mode is good for novice players.
When you press the L1 button to aim the weapon, 
the crosshairs automatically lock on to an enemy 
within range. However, you cannot attack specific 
parts of the body.


While in Auto Aim Mode, "AUTO AIM" is displayed 
at the top center of the screen.




Press the □ button to switch to 
Over-the-Shoulder Mode, 
and the △ button to switch to First Person Mode.

ATTACK ACTIONS 1


Over-the-Shoulder Mode




When you press the L1 button to aim the weapon, 
the camera switches to a diagonal view 
from behind the character.



Use the right stick to adjust the aim. 
Push the R3 button in to switch the view 
between left and right.



Aiming is not as precise as in First Person Mode.

Press the □ button to switch to Auto Aim Mode, 
and the △ button to switch to First Person Mode.

ATTACK ACTIONS 1


First Person Mode




When you press the L1 button to aim the weapon 
and then press the △ button, the camera switches 
to the character's perspective.
Use the right stick to adjust the aim.


First Person Mode allows for 
a high degree of aiming precision.

Press the △ button to return to the previous mode.

ATTACK ACTIONS 1
Lock On Distance

Lock on distance in Auto Aim Mode varies
according to weapon.
Submachine guns have the longest range, followed
by handguns, assault rifles, and shotguns.
Other attributes also vary according to weapon,
such as destructive power and recoil.

Get to know the differences between each weapon
 and find ones that work best for you.

ATTACK ACTIONS 2
Here you will learn the controls for CQC.

* You need to equip the "CQC+" skill to use CQC. 
If you do not have it equipped, 
exit Training and equip the skill under 
"Skill Settings" in "Personal."

When you equip a weapon, a "CQC" mark 
on the lower right of the screen tells you 
that the weapon can be used with CQC.



Each weapon is slightly different, but in general, 
tapping the R1 button rapidly executes a melee attack, 
while pressing and holding the R1 button executes 
a grab attack.


While holding an enemy, you can move around, shoot, 
and perform a variety of other actions. 
Go ahead and experiment.

Choose "all" (all players) or "team" (teammates only) 
with the left/right directional buttons and 
use the keyboard to enter a message.



Please refrain from sending messages 
that may upset other players.

This is the START button Menu

Here you can view the map and rules, 
and change game options.
* You cannot change skill settings here.



To switch to a different type of training, 
select TRAINING, then select the category 
you want to train in.

To quit training, select QUIT.

BASIC ACTIONS


Here you can practice movements and camera controls.
Movement controls are as follows:



Use the left stick to move.
Movement speed changes depending 
on how much you tilt the stick.



Press the × button to switch between 
standing and crouching.
Press the × button longer to switch between 
standing and lying down.


Press the × button while running to execute a roll.

Press the △ button while lying down to switch between 
lying face up and face down.

BASIC ACTIONS


Camera controls are as follows:




Use the right stick to rotate the camera.

Press the R3 button to move the camera angle 
to behind the character's back.


Quickly press the R3 button in twice to move 
the camera angle to behind the character's back 
and reset the vertical angle to the default setting.

ATTACK ACTIONS 1


Here you will learn the controls for attacking.




Each weapon is slightly different, but in general, 
the L1 button is used to aim and the R1 button 
is used to fire.
Press the ○ button to reload.
For more details, see the descriptions for each weapon.

ATTACK ACTIONS 1


Before getting to attack methods, 
let's look at how to distinguish between friend and foe.



- Distinguishing Between Friend and Foe -
To tell friend from foe in a Team Battle, 
look to see whether the character's name 
is displayed above them.
Allies always have their names displayed. 

Enemies' names will only be displayed 
when you aim a weapon at them.

In this training, you are assigned to the Blue Team.
The dummies in this stage are also divided into teams. 

Look at how their names are displayed.

You can attack enemies, 
but be careful: if you attack an ally, 
your weapon will be locked for a while.

ATTACK ACTIONS 1

Next, you will learn about the 3 attack modes:  
Auto Aim, Over-the-Shoulder, and First Person.




Auto Aim Mode

Auto Aim Mode can only be used if Lock-On 
Settings is Enabled in GamePlay Options.

This mode is good for novice players.
When you press the L1 button to aim the weapon, 
the crosshairs automatically lock on to an enemy 
within range. However, you cannot attack specific 
parts of the body.


While in Auto Aim Mode, "AUTO AIM" is displayed 
at the top center of the screen.




Press the □ button to switch to 
Over-the-Shoulder Mode, 
and the △ button to switch to First Person Mode.

ATTACK ACTIONS 1


Over-the-Shoulder Mode




When you press the L1 button to aim the weapon, 
the camera switches to a diagonal view 
from behind the character.



Use the right stick to adjust the aim. 
Push the R3 button in to switch the view 
between left and right.



Aiming is not as precise as in First Person Mode.

Press the □ button to switch to Auto Aim Mode, 
and the △ button to switch to First Person Mode.

ATTACK ACTIONS 1


First Person Mode




When you press the L1 button to aim the weapon 
and then press the △ button, the camera switches 
to the character's perspective.
Use the right stick to adjust the aim.


First Person Mode allows for 
a high degree of aiming precision.

Press the △ button to return to the previous mode.

ATTACK ACTIONS 1
Lock On Distance

Lock on distance in Auto Aim Mode varies
according to weapon.
Submachine guns have the longest range, followed
by handguns, assault rifles, and shotguns.
Other attributes also vary according to weapon,
such as destructive power and recoil.

Get to know the differences between each weapon
 and find ones that work best for you.

While holding an enemy, you can move around, shoot, 
and perform a variety of other actions. 
Go ahead and experiment.

EQUIPMENT OPERATIONS


To switch weapons or items during the game, 
use the R2 button for weapons and the L2 button for items.



The window will stay on the screen as long as 
you hold down the corresponding button. 
Use the left stick or directional buttons 
to make your selection.



You can also view weapon and item descriptions 
and controls in this window.



Alternately, you can do a Quick Change by tapping 
the R2 button or the L2 button.

This is the START button Menu

Here you can view the map and rules, 
and change game options.
* You cannot change skill settings here.



To switch to a different type of training, 
select TRAINING, then select the category 
you want to train in.

To quit training, select QUIT.

BASIC ACTIONS


Here you can practice movements and camera controls.
Movement controls are as follows:



Use the left stick to move.
Movement speed changes depending 
on how much you tilt the stick.



Press the × button to switch between 
standing and crouching.
Press the × button longer to switch between 
standing and lying down.


Press the × button while running to execute a roll.

Press the △ button while lying down to switch between 
lying face up and face down.

BASIC ACTIONS


Camera controls are as follows:




Use the right stick to rotate the camera.

Press the R3 button to move the camera angle 
to behind the character's back.


Quickly press the R3 button in twice to move 
the camera angle to behind the character's back 
and reset the vertical angle to the default setting.

ATTACK ACTIONS 1


Here you will learn the controls for attacking.




Each weapon is slightly different, but in general, 
the L1 button is used to aim and the R1 button 
is used to fire.
Press the ○ button to reload.
For more details, see the descriptions for each weapon.

ATTACK ACTIONS 1


Before getting to attack methods, 
let's look at how to distinguish between friend and foe.



- Distinguishing Between Friend and Foe -
To tell friend from foe in a Team Battle, 
look to see whether the character's name 
is displayed above them.
Allies always have their names displayed. 

Enemies' names will only be displayed 
when you aim a weapon at them.

In this training, you are assigned to the Blue Team.
The dummies in this stage are also divided into teams. 

Look at how their names are displayed.

You can attack enemies, 
but be careful: if you attack an ally, 
your weapon will be locked for a while.

ATTACK ACTIONS 1

Next, you will learn about the 3 attack modes:  
Auto Aim, Over-the-Shoulder, and First Person.




Auto Aim Mode

Auto Aim Mode can only be used if Lock-On 
Settings is Enabled in GamePlay Options.

This mode is good for novice players.
When you press the L1 button to aim the weapon, 
the crosshairs automatically lock on to an enemy 
within range. However, you cannot attack specific 
parts of the body.


While in Auto Aim Mode, "AUTO AIM" is displayed 
at the top center of the screen.




Press the □ button to switch to 
Over-the-Shoulder Mode, 
and the △ button to switch to First Person Mode.

ATTACK ACTIONS 1


Over-the-Shoulder Mode




When you press the L1 button to aim the weapon, 
the camera switches to a diagonal view 
from behind the character.



Use the right stick to adjust the aim. 
Push the R3 button in to switch the view 
between left and right.



Aiming is not as precise as in First Person Mode.

Press the □ button to switch to Auto Aim Mode, 
and the △ button to switch to First Person Mode.

ATTACK ACTIONS 1


First Person Mode




When you press the L1 button to aim the weapon 
and then press the △ button, the camera switches 
to the character's perspective.
Use the right stick to adjust the aim.


First Person Mode allows for 
a high degree of aiming precision.

Press the △ button to return to the previous mode.

ATTACK ACTIONS 1
Lock On Distance

Lock on distance in Auto Aim Mode varies
according to weapon.
Submachine guns have the longest range, followed
by handguns, assault rifles, and shotguns.
Other attributes also vary according to weapon,
such as destructive power and recoil.

Get to know the differences between each weapon
 and find ones that work best for you.

ATTACK ACTIONS 2
Here you will learn the controls for CQC.

* You need to equip the "CQC+" skill to use CQC. 
If you do not have it equipped, 
exit Training and equip the skill under 
"Skill Settings" in "Personal."

When you equip a weapon, a "CQC" mark 
on the lower right of the screen tells you 
that the weapon can be used with CQC.



Each weapon is slightly different, but in general, 
tapping the R1 button rapidly executes a melee attack, 
while pressing and holding the R1 button executes 
a grab attack.


While holding an enemy, you can move around, shoot, 
and perform a variety of other actions. 
Go ahead and experiment.

This mode is good for novice players.

First Person Mode




When you press the L1 button to aim the weapon 
and then press the △ button, the camera switches 
to the character's perspective.

First Person Mode allows for 
a high degree of aiming precision.

Press the △ button to return to the previous mode.

ATTACK ACTIONS 1


Here you will learn the controls for attacking.




Each weapon is slightly different, but in general, 
the L1 button is used to aim and the R1 button

Press the ○ button to reload.
For more details, see the descriptions for each weapon.

ATTACK ACTIONS 1


Before getting to attack methods, 
let's look at how to distinguish between friend and foe.



- Distinguishing Between Friend and Foe -
To tell friend from foe in a Team Battle, 
look to see whether the character's name 
is displayed above them.
Allies always have their names displayed. 

Enemies' names will only be displayed 
when you aim a weapon at them.

In this training, you are assigned to the Blue Team.
The dummies in this stage are also divided into teams. 

Look at how their names are displayed.

You can attack enemies, 
but be careful: if you attack an ally, 
your weapon will be locked for a while.

ATTACK ACTIONS 1

Next, you will learn about the 3 attack modes:  
Auto Aim, Over-the-Shoulder, and First Person.




Auto Aim Mode

Auto Aim Mode can only be used if Lock-On 
Settings is Enabled in GamePlay Options.

This mode is good for novice players.
When you press the L1 button to aim the weapon, 
the crosshairs automatically lock on to an enemy 
within range. However, you cannot attack specific 
parts of the body.


While in Auto Aim Mode, "AUTO AIM" is displayed 
at the top center of the screen.




Press the □ button to switch to 
Over-the-Shoulder Mode, 
and the △ button to switch to First Person Mode.

ATTACK ACTIONS 1


Over-the-Shoulder Mode




When you press the L1 button to aim the weapon, 
the camera switches to a diagonal view 
from behind the character.



Use the right stick to adjust the aim. 
Push the R3 button in to switch the view 
between left and right.



Aiming is not as precise as in First Person Mode.

Press the □ button to switch to Auto Aim Mode, 
and the △ button to switch to First Person Mode.

ATTACK ACTIONS 1


First Person Mode




When you press the L1 button to aim the weapon 
and then press the △ button, the camera switches 
to the character's perspective.
Use the right stick to adjust the aim.


First Person Mode allows for 
a high degree of aiming precision.

Press the △ button to return to the previous mode.

ATTACK ACTIONS 1
Lock On Distance

Lock on distance in Auto Aim Mode varies
according to weapon.
Submachine guns have the longest range, followed
by handguns, assault rifles, and shotguns.
Other attributes also vary according to weapon,
such as destructive power and recoil.

Get to know the differences between each weapon
 and find ones that work best for you.

ATTACK ACTIONS 2
Here you will learn the controls for CQC.

* You need to equip the "CQC+" skill to use CQC.

Auto Aim Mode can only be used if Lock-On

This mode is good for novice players.
When you press the L1 button to aim the weapon, 
the crosshairs automatically lock on to an enemy 
within range. However, you cannot attack specific 
parts of the body.


While in Auto Aim Mode, "AUTO AIM" is displayed 
at the top center of the screen.

Over-the-Shoulder Mode




When you press the L1 button to aim the weapon, 
the camera switches to a diagonal view 
from behind the character.



Use the right stick to adjust the aim. 
Push the R3 button in to switch the view 
between left and right.



Aiming is not as precise as in First Person Mode.

Press the □ button to switch to Auto Aim Mode, 
and the △ button to switch to First Person Mode.

ATTACK ACTIONS 1


First Person Mode




When you press the L1 button to aim the weapon 
and then press the △ button, the camera switches 
to the character's perspective.
Use the right stick to adjust the aim.


First Person Mode allows for 
a high degree of aiming precision.

Press the △ button to return to the previous mode.

BASIC ACTIONS


Here you can practice movements and camera controls.
Movement controls are as follows:



Use the left stick to move.
Movement speed changes depending 
on how much you tilt the stick.



Press the × button to switch between 
standing and crouching.
Press the × button longer to switch between 
standing and lying down.

Press the △ button while lying down to switch between 
lying face up and face down.

BASIC ACTIONS


Camera controls are as follows:




Use the right stick to rotate the camera.

Press the R3 button to move the camera angle 
to behind the character's back.


Quickly press the R3 button in twice to move 
the camera angle to behind the character's back 
and reset the vertical angle to the default setting.

ATTACK ACTIONS 1


Here you will learn the controls for attacking.




Each weapon is slightly different, but in general, 
the L1 button is used to aim and the R1 button 
is used to fire.
Press the ○ button to reload.
For more details, see the descriptions for each weapon.

ATTACK ACTIONS 1


Before getting to attack methods, 
let's look at how to distinguish between friend and foe.



- Distinguishing Between Friend and Foe -
To tell friend from foe in a Team Battle, 
look to see whether the character's name 
is displayed above them.
Allies always have their names displayed. 

Enemies' names will only be displayed 
when you aim a weapon at them.

In this training, you are assigned to the Blue Team.
The dummies in this stage are also divided into teams. 

Look at how their names are displayed.

You can attack enemies, 
but be careful: if you attack an ally, 
your weapon will be locked for a while.

ATTACK ACTIONS 1

Next, you will learn about the 3 attack modes:  
Auto Aim, Over-the-Shoulder, and First Person.




Auto Aim Mode

Auto Aim Mode can only be used if Lock-On 
Settings is Enabled in GamePlay Options.

This mode is good for novice players.
When you press the L1 button to aim the weapon, 
the crosshairs automatically lock on to an enemy 
within range. However, you cannot attack specific 
parts of the body.


While in Auto Aim Mode, "AUTO AIM" is displayed 
at the top center of the screen.




Press the □ button to switch to 
Over-the-Shoulder Mode, 
and the △ button to switch to First Person Mode.

ATTACK ACTIONS 1


Over-the-Shoulder Mode




When you press the L1 button to aim the weapon, 
the camera switches to a diagonal view 
from behind the character.



Use the right stick to adjust the aim. 
Push the R3 button in to switch the view 
between left and right.



Aiming is not as precise as in First Person Mode.

Press the □ button to switch to Auto Aim Mode, 
and the △ button to switch to First Person Mode.

ATTACK ACTIONS 1


First Person Mode




When you press the L1 button to aim the weapon 
and then press the △ button, the camera switches 
to the character's perspective.
Use the right stick to adjust the aim.


First Person Mode allows for 
a high degree of aiming precision.

Press the △ button to return to the previous mode.

ATTACK ACTIONS 1
Lock On Distance

Lock on distance in Auto Aim Mode varies
according to weapon.
Submachine guns have the longest range, followed
by handguns, assault rifles, and shotguns.
Other attributes also vary according to weapon,
such as destructive power and recoil.

Get to know the differences between each weapon
 and find ones that work best for you.
